editorial:
Imagine being a low-level street thug who suddenly wakes up in the shoes of a powerful mob boss. That is exactly what happens to Mickey Skinner. Through a crazy set of events, he goes from being a nobody to running a brutal London gang right as they are about to make a massive amount of money from a human-trafficking deal. The vibe is gritty and tense, making you feel the pressure Mickey is under as he tries to fake his way through a world where one wrong word could get him killed. It is a wild ride that mixes crime drama with a lot of stress.

You will love how the movie keeps you guessing if Mickey will get caught or actually pull it off. The acting is solid, and the pacing moves quick enough to keep you from getting bored. While some of the plot points feel a bit lucky, the tension makes up for it. If you enjoy crime stories with a big twist, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Mickey manages to navigate the dangerous waters of the gang, but the ride is far from smooth. The big twist reveals that his rise to power was not just luck, but a series of calculations and betrayals. He eventually secures the money and the power he wanted, though he loses his innocence along the way. The movie wraps up with Mickey fully embracing his new, darker identity as a leader in the underworld.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog stories and gritty crime thrillers.
similarMovies: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
